title: BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Generating 40 Billion Daily Bid Requests Disrupted
content_md: Bot and fraud protection firm Human Security says it has disrupted the largest ad fraud botnet by bid volume. Dubbed BadBox 3.0 , it is the third iteration of a large operation targeting low-cost Android devices. The first BadBox botnet ensnared more than 190,000 devices , while BadBox 2.0 was initially found on over 1 million devices, but eventually ensnared more than 10 million . “At its height, BadBox 3.0 accounted for roughly 40 billion bid requests a day and more than 4% of all CTV traffic observed by the Human Defense Platform,” Human Security says , noting the bid request volume was three times the volume recorded for the VastFlux ad fraud scheme. Portions of BadBox 3.0, the cybersecurity firm says, were operated via command-and-control (C&C) domains that were disrupted when Google took down XCPE , a botnet of over 1.3 million Android set-top boxes. The botnet consists of low-cost, uncertified Android Open Source Project devices infected with backdoors delivering fraud modules designed to render hidden video ads and to enroll the devices into residential proxy networks. Human Security says its Satori Threat Intelligence and Research Team has uncovered an actively maintained catalog of fraud modules hosted on public repositories, as well as links to Chinese electronics manufacturer TXCZ.
